subject: Human Evolution
title: Health and Ancestry
description: A short lesson to help you apply Health and Ancestry.

hook.text: Some genetic diseases cluster in specific populations—not because of race, but because of shared ancestral history.

buildup.text: Tay-Sachs in Ashkenazi Jews, cystic fibrosis in Northern Europeans—founder effects concentrated rare variants.

discovery.text: Understanding ancestral genetics helps doctors predict risk and tailor treatments for specific populations.

twist.text: But most disease risk is shared across all humans. Population-specific risks are the exception, not the rule.

climax.text: Ancestry-informed medicine must balance genetic insight with the danger of reinforcing racial categories.

punchline.text: Ancestry matters for health, but less than you think.

quiz.question: Why do some genetic diseases cluster in specific populations?
options: Founder effects concentrated rare gene variants in isolated groups
